body.title: Describe Autonomous Health as an integrated AI health system
body.body:
## What changed

- README and component contract: Autonomous Health is an AI health system integrated with each person's UID, Dk Personal, personal Dknowledge and devices, with AI-run clinics, investigating patterns with sufficient probability for multifactor detection.
- Professional review alongside AI diagnosis and monitoring.
- The open questions no longer ask what a health application would do, but how Autonomous Health would be built step by step.
- llms.txt: Drayker is the supersystem.

## Founder

> "o sistema está integrado ao Dk pessoal e ao dknowledge da pessoa, mais seus dispositivos, padrões que podem estar conectados a algo com probabilidade suficiente são investigados… além de salvar vidas também aprimora a detecção multifator de todo tipo de condição."

> "Ela não é definível, a única definição que cabe é de super sistema."

body.title: open-science: Autonomous Health is an AI health system tied to UID and Dk Personal
body.body:
## What changes
- **README:** Autonomous Health is described as the health system this work is meant to build: clinics run with artificial intelligence and integrated with each person's UID and Dk Personal, a diagnostic intelligence that learns from every examination, a treatment intelligence that draws on the whole body of studies and learns from outcomes, and the person's Dk following their health over time. Clinics and doctors take part through registered identities. None of this operates today.
- **Not in scope:** "Clinical autonomy of any kind, whatever the internal project name suggests" is removed. The medical-service line now says "today".
- **component.yml:** the same, plus Autonomous Health in the scope.

## Why
The previous wording redefined the name and excluded the founder's design. The honest current state stays.

body.title: Demonstrate evidence organization on one non-clinical question
body.body:
## What is delivered
One non-clinical research question, and a demonstration that does only this: search, explain, or organize existing evidence about it. On synthetic data, reviewed by someone with domain expertise.

Written up so a reader can see what was done, what the limits were, and where it would break.

## Why it is needed
This repository describes a domain where overreach is not a style problem — it is a safety problem. There is no clinical protocol, no validation, no dataset, no device, no regulatory approval and no safety evidence, and the honest first step is deliberately unglamorous.

Doing the small version well is what earns the right to describe anything larger.

## Where to start
Non-clinical means the output cannot be read as being about a particular person's health. Organizing published findings on a research question qualifies; anything resembling a diagnosis, a recommendation or a triage does not.

The specialist review is part of the deliverable, not a formality after it.

## Prior material

Drayker has earlier work on this subject in its own knowledge base — drafts, mostly in Portuguese, written before the public repositories took their current shape. It is not published yet. If you take this function, say so in the thread and the relevant material will be published alongside it, so you are consolidating and arguing with existing thinking rather than starting from a blank page.

---
This is an open function: small enough for one person to finish, defined enough that the result composes with the rest. Claim it in this thread before starting so two people do not carry the same function, and deliver through a pull request to `master`. It appears on the board at https://drayker.org/fn/
